quotes_checked: 27 of 27 exact (3 agreed, 8+8+8 in readings); the cited-in-answers and terms verses (Gen 25:23 not fetched; John 12:32, Amos 3:2, Rom 9:8, Acts 4:28, 1 Cor 2:7, 2 Pet 1:10, 1 Pet 1:1, Col 3:12) also match

fixes.why: The writer left the textual variant open. Ancient manuscripts divide between 'from the beginning' and 'as firstfruits'. The Berean follows the first, and the card puts the verse in the common ground, so a reader who knows the variant would find it unmarked. The Berean's own marginal note belongs on the page.
fixes.fix: Keep the quote and add a short marker on the passage: 'Some ancient manuscripts read “as firstfruits” in place of “from the beginning”.'

fixes.why: In Isaiah the servant is named Israel in the same section (Isaiah 41:8; 49:3), so reading the verse as the Chosen One who is Christ is the New Testament's use of it, which Matthew 12:18 makes. The note should say whose reading it is and keep the Isaianic sense visible, so the card does not read the verse as Isaiah alone settling a Christian claim.
fixes.fix: Replace the note with: 'In Isaiah the servant is also called Israel (Isaiah 41:8, 49:3); holders of this reading follow Matthew 12:18 in taking this verse of Christ, the Chosen One.'

fixes.why: In Ezekiel the verse answers a complaint about Israel's own fortunes in exile and is about the repentance of the wicked, not about election. It enters this debate only because holders of the first reading cite it, and the note states it as bare fact.
fixes.fix: Replace the note with: 'Cited by holders of this reading: God's stated pleasure is in the turning and living of the wicked.'

fixes.why: The second reading's summary says 'others in those traditions hold the first' of Anglican and Baptist members, but Anglican is not in the first reading's held_by. Arminian Anglicans (the Wesleyan line arose in the Church of England) hold it. The two lists contradict each other as written.
fixes.fix: Add "Anglican" to the first reading's held_by, and add to its summary: 'Many Anglican members hold this reading, and members differ among themselves.'

fixes.why: The summary says 'Some Reformed and Lutheran members give weight to election in Christ beside the second reading', but neither is in held_by. The summary then describes members of traditions outside the list. A reader checking the list against the prose finds a mismatch (the writer's own unresolved note).
fixes.fix: Either add "Reformed" and "Lutheran" to held_by with the summary kept as written (it already says they hold it beside the second), or cut the sentence. The first is closer to how the traditions describe themselves.

fixes.where: terms: conditional election, corporate election, unconditional election
fixes.why: The terms are labels from later systematic debate, not the text's words and not the early church's. The notes do not say this, and 'the Reformed term' for unconditional election is a stylised summary of a tradition that does not state the doctrine in those words in every confession. A scholar will want the labels marked as post-biblical classification.
fixes.fix: Add to the notes for conditional, unconditional and corporate election the sentence: 'This is a label from later theological discussion, not a word of the text.'

fixes.why: The writer's own list of left-out verses names Ephesians 1:11 and the verses of the Father's giving. Ephesians 1:11 sits inside the same long sentence as the agreed Ephesians 1:4 and 1:5 and is among the verses holders of this reading cite first. John 15:16 is the verse most often quoted for the choosing coming first from God.
fixes.fix: Add to reading 2, replacing none (reading 2 then has 9; add one to each other reading, see next two fixes): {"ref": "Ephesians 1:11", "quote": "In Him we were also chosen as God's own, having been predestined according to the plan of Him who works out everything by the counsel of His will,", "note": "The choosing and predestining are placed in God's plan and counsel."}. If the count must stay at 8, swap in John 15:16 for Acts 13:48 (which both readings already treat in their answers): {"ref": "John 15:16", "quote": "You did not choose Me, but I chose you.", "note": "The choosing begins with Christ."}

fixes.why: Romans 9-11 builds toward the end of chapter 11, and the first and third readings cite its close, which neither list gives. It also puts Israel's present standing on the card without a sentence on it. Romans 11:5 gives the chosen-by-grace remnant to the third reading.
fixes.fix: Add to reading 1: {"ref": "Romans 11:32", "quote": "For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.", "note": "The arc of Romans 9-11 ends in mercy for everyone."}. Add to reading 3: {"ref": "Romans 11:5", "quote": "In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.", "note": "A chosen remnant within Israel, chosen by grace."}

fixes.why: Verses 6 and 7 are one argument, and the card splits it between two readings. This is fair only if each note says the other half is there too. A reader of one reading alone sees half of Moses's sentence.
fixes.fix: Add to the end of each note: 'Deuteronomy 7:6-8 is read whole by both readings.' (7:8 gives God's love and oath as the ground, which neither reading disputes.)

summary: All 27 quotes are the Berean's exact words, the readings are in their holders' terms, and no verdict or weighted word appears in the writer's text. The fixes mark the 2 Thessalonians 13 variant, state whose reading the Old Testament notes are, correct the Anglican and Reformed/Lutheran held_by mismatches, label the post-biblical terms, and add Ephesians 1:11, Romans 11:32 and Romans 11:5.
